events.title: Duke of Burgundy Assassinated at Montereau
events.description: John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, was killed by supporters of the Dauphin, the future Charles VII of France. He died during a supposed peace meeting.
events.significance: The murder deepened the feud between the Burgundians and the Armagnacs during the Hundred Years' War. It pushed Burgundy into an alliance with England.

events.title: Battle of Pinkie
events.description: English forces under Edward VI's regime decisively defeated a Scottish army. It was the last full-scale battle between the two kingdoms.
events.significance: The battle marked the end of an era of open warfare between England and Scotland. It was part of the 'Rough Wooing' over the future marriage of Mary, Queen of Scots.

events.title: Elias Howe Patents the Sewing Machine
events.description: American inventor Elias Howe was granted a patent for his sewing machine. It used a lockstitch design with the thread passing through the needle's eye at the point.
events.significance: The machine helped transform clothing manufacture and the textile industry. It became a landmark of the Industrial Revolution.

events.title: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye Signed
events.description: The Republic of German-Austria signed the treaty with the Allied powers after World War I. Austria gave up significant territory to Italy, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia.
events.significance: The treaty formally dissolved the Austro-Hungarian Empire's old order and redrew the map of Central Europe.
